text: Thomasson's 'easy ontology' holds that whether ordinary tables exist can be answered only by a deep metaphysical investigation into what is fundamental.
explanation: False. Thomasson's easy ontology says such questions are answered easily, by applying ordinary conceptual/application rules to uncontested facts (there is wood arranged table-wise, so there is a table). It is the heavyweight realist (Sider) who reserves substantive investigation for questions of fundamentality and structure.
